name: Haus Morgenlicht
description: An old chalet. A new way to live. Air, light and mountain views, through summer and winter.

budget.label: Conversion construction package
budget.note: €92,000 structure/replanning + €98,000 roof/fabric + €58,000 building services. Subquotes included once.

budget.label: Structural adaptations & replanning
budget.note: Included in Alpen Bauatelier. Local openings, supports, selective partitions and making good; technical design required.

budget.label: Roof renewal & envelope insulation
budget.note: Included in main construction. Preserve roof geometry; renewed weathering layers and insulation allowance. Glazing separately priced.

budget.label: Building services coordination
budget.note: Included in construction: €24,000 electrical + €34,000 heating/ventilation. Decorative light fixtures excluded.

budget.label: Electrical installation & controls
budget.note: Second-tier included subquote within Haus Technik and Alpen Bauatelier. Do not add again.

budget.label: Heating & ventilation package
budget.note: Included in Haus Technik. System selection and performance follow specialist design; no energy rating is promised.

budget.label: Windows, doors & enlarged view openings
budget.note: €64,000 glazing supply + €40,000 frames, installation and detailing. Structural opening work is in Berg Struktur.

budget.label: Glazing fabrication package
budget.note: Included in Panorama Werk. Fabrication allowance pending thermal, structural and safety specifications.

budget.label: Kitchen & bespoke silver-fir joinery
budget.note: €62,000 cabinetry, worktops and fitting + €16,000 appliances. Includes arrival storage and selected bedroom joinery.

budget.label: Integrated kitchen appliances
budget.note: Included in Fir Atelier; final equipment schedule to be selected.

budget.label: Timber floors, plaster & stone finishes
budget.note: General interior floor and wall finishes. Kitchen worktops and bathroom vanity are in their own packages.

budget.label: Furniture, curtains & textiles
budget.note: Base selection €42,000; premium upholstery, rugs and loose furniture €58,000. Terrace option separate.

budget.label: Decorative lighting
budget.note: Decorative fixture supply only; installation and controls included in Lichtwerk Tirol.

budget.label: Main bathrooms & sanitary fixtures
budget.note: Main-house sanitaryware, fittings and vanity package. Optional wellness suite excluded.

budget.label: Architecture, interiors & coordination allowance
budget.note: Concept, design development, coordination and eight site reviews. Statutory fees, measured surveys and specialist reports excluded.

budget.label: Alpine access & site logistics
budget.note: Staged delivery and access allowance. Extraordinary weather delay and road restrictions remain outside this fixed demo allowance.

budget.label: Client-held renovation contingency
budget.note: Uncommitted client reserve for a fictional conversion; not a supplier charge or permission to spend.

budget.label: Optional garden-level wellness suite
budget.note: Illustrated wellness room is optional and off by default. €20,000 room fit-out + €14,800 sauna subquote.

budget.label: Sauna cabin & heater package
budget.note: Included in optional Waldwasser package. Parent selection controls whether this scope is enabled; never add twice.

budget.label: Optional terrace lounge & wind screens
budget.note: Loose outdoor seating and wind-screen allowance, additional to base terrace making good. Terrace image shows this option.

budget.label: Concealed timber defects & unforeseen ground work
budget.note: Unknown and excluded from all totals until opened up and assessed. Not a zero-cost allowance.

slides.title:
Haus
Morgenlicht.
slides.subtitle: AN OLD CHALET. A NEW WAY TO LIVE.
slides.body: Air, light and the mountains. A fictional Austrian chalet conversion / September 2026

slides.title:
A new chapter,
with an old soul.
slides.subtitle: 01 / THE INVITATION
slides.body: For fictional clients Anna and Lukas Leitner, the chalet becomes a generous retreat in every season: open to summer meadows, warm against winter snow, and always connected to the mountains.
points: Imagined location: the Tyrolean Alps, Austria
Illustrative 280 m² interior concept across three levels

slides.title:
Leave room
for the view.
slides.subtitle: THE FEELING
slides.body: Morning air. A clear horizon. The quiet of the mountains before the day begins. The design brings that sense of space indoors through light, calm materials and carefully framed views.

slides.title:
A house worth
keeping.
slides.subtitle: 02 / THE IMAGINED ORIGINAL
slides.body: A weathered timber chalet with a generous pitched roof, a stone base and a heavy carved balcony. Its character is the starting point. This is an AI-generated fictional existing-condition study, not a site survey photograph.

slides.title:
Warm character.
Closed-off rooms.
slides.subtitle: THE ORIGINAL INTERIOR
slides.body: Dark beams, orange-toned panelling, compact windows and substantial furniture make the imagined living room feel inward-looking. The green tiled stove is a beautiful anchor for its next chapter.

slides.title:
Keep the soul.
Open the possibilities.
slides.subtitle: THE CONVERSION STRATEGY
slides.body: Retain the elements that give the chalet its identity. Introduce contemporary comfort through deliberate, local changes.
points: Keep the roof silhouette, stone plinth and sound beams
Restore the tiled stove and selected weathered timber
Open the valley facade and selected internal partitions
Lighten the envelope with pale fir and warm plaster

slides.title:
Same silhouette.
New light.
slides.subtitle: BEFORE / PROPOSED EXTERIOR
slides.body: A matched concept edit keeps the camera position, roof geometry and landscape recognisable while exploring a lighter facade, simpler balcony and larger view openings. Both images are fictional generated studies.

slides.title:
The familiar form,
made clear.
slides.subtitle: 3D / CHALET EXTERIOR
slides.body: A classic architectural render studies the retained roof, timber balcony and stone base alongside the enlarged glazing. Faceted mountains and simplified trees keep the proposed building in focus.

slides.title:
Mountain materials.
A lighter touch.
slides.subtitle: 03 / MATERIAL MOOD
slides.body: Weathered old timber meets pale silver fir, warm ivory plaster and cool grey-green stone. Brushed metal provides a quiet line of detail. Texture does the work that ornament once did.

slides.title:
The warmth
you can feel.
slides.subtitle: TEXTILE & COLOUR MOOD
slides.body: Ivory wool, oatmeal linen, glacier blue and a small rust accent. Softness belongs to the interior; the mountain view brings all the drama we need.

slides.title:
Snow. Stone.
Sky. Timber.
slides.subtitle: THE COLOUR LANGUAGE
slides.body: A fresh, pale foundation with mineral blues and the warmth of timber. Existing dark beams remain deliberate lines within the lighter rooms.

slides.title:
Understand the
original rhythm.
slides.subtitle: 04 / EXISTING LAYOUT STUDY
slides.body: An imagined main-floor arrangement of separate kitchen, dining, living and arrival rooms. The plan is a storytelling device based on the fictional brief; it is not an existing measured drawing.

slides.title:
Open the rooms.
Keep the refuge.
slides.subtitle: PROPOSED MAIN FLOOR
slides.body: Connected cooking, dining and living face the valley, while storage, stairs and practical arrival functions stay contained. Enlarged openings and partition changes require site-specific structural design.

slides.title:
The mountains,
invited inside.
slides.subtitle: THE REIMAGINED LIVING ROOM
slides.body: The original beam rhythm and green tiled stove remain. Pale surfaces, softer furniture and a larger valley-facing opening make the same room feel open, generous and full of air.

slides.title:
Old rhythm.
New openness.
slides.subtitle: 3D / LIVING ROOM MODEL
slides.body: A shaded interior model brings the beams, green tiled stove and new view opening into one composition. Simple materials make the room proportions and furniture arrangement easy to discuss.

slides.title:
The same room.
A different feeling.
slides.subtitle: BEFORE / PROPOSED LIVING
slides.body: A matched interior edit retains the camera, room boundaries, beams and stove. The transformation comes from daylight, restrained joinery and furniture that allows the space to breathe.

slides.title:
Light follows
the roofline.
slides.subtitle: SECTION / THE SPATIAL IDEA
slides.body: Retain the pitched roof and work with its volume. New view openings and lighter ceiling infill bring daylight deeper into the chalet; the garden level holds service space and an optional wellness retreat.

slides.title:
Breakfast,
with a horizon.
slides.subtitle: KITCHEN & DINING
slides.body: Pale silver-fir cabinetry, a mineral stone island and an unhurried dining table create the social heart. Old dark beams keep the room grounded in the original chalet.

slides.title:
Fewer materials.
More meaning.
slides.subtitle: DETAILS & SPECIFICATION
slides.body: Joinery, plaster and stone repeat through the house. Every material meets an older element somewhere, making the conversion feel connected rather than newly assembled.

slides.title:
Wake up
above the noise.
slides.subtitle: THE PRIMARY SUITE
slides.body: A light-filled room beneath the gable, with wool, soft blue and a view of winter peaks. Retained beams frame the pitched ceiling; the new glazing makes the landscape part of the room.

slides.title:
Quiet rooms,
under the eaves.
slides.subtitle: UPPER FLOOR CONCEPT
slides.body: A primary suite, guest room and shared landing are organised around the existing roof form. Gable openings, headroom and escape arrangements remain subject to measured and technical review.

slides.title:
For snowy boots
and muddy adventures.
slides.subtitle: THE PRACTICAL ARRIVAL
slides.body: Pale built-in storage, a soft bench and durable mineral flooring make coming home easy. A calm place to leave skis, walking boots and the weather before entering the living rooms.

slides.title:
Warmth,
after the mountain.
slides.subtitle: OPTIONAL WELLNESS RETREAT
slides.body: A quiet garden-level room of stone, timber and soft winter light. The illustrated €34,800 wellness suite is optional, including its €14,800 sauna package; it is unselected in the base budget.

slides.title:
Summer lives
with the doors open.
slides.subtitle: 05 / THE SUMMER CHALET
slides.body: Meadow greens, cool stone and the long light of the Alps. The reworked facade opens generously while retaining the familiar chalet silhouette and its relationship with the slope.

slides.title:
Take the slow
way through the day.
slides.subtitle: THE SUMMER TERRACE
slides.body: A sheltered place for coffee, reading and looking outward. The furniture and wind-screen treatment shown belong to the optional €12,600 terrace package.

slides.title:
A warm light
in a white landscape.
slides.subtitle: THE WINTER CHALET
slides.body: The same renovated chalet, held in snow and evening blue. Warm rooms glow behind the new glazing; timber and stone keep the building rooted in its Alpine setting.

slides.title:
One home.
Two beautiful worlds.
slides.subtitle: SUMMER / WINTER
slides.body: Seasonal studies of the same proposed exterior. The architecture stays constant; light, landscape and daily rituals change around it.

slides.title:
Comfort begins
with the building.
slides.subtitle: FABRIC, AIR & LIGHT
slides.body: Roof and envelope work, carefully specified glazing, and coordinated heating and ventilation support the architectural concept. Actual performance follows surveys, specialist design and commissioning.

slides.title:
A clear view
of the conversion.
slides.subtitle: 06 / THE INVESTMENT
slides.body: €687,500–€703,500 including a €62,000 client-held contingency. Furniture choices create the range. Optional wellness and terrace packages are excluded; concealed defects remain unpriced. Figures are fictional and include assumed VAT.

slides.title:
Every package.
Every layer.
slides.subtitle: THE SUPPLIER STRUCTURE
slides.body: Included subquotes explain their parent price. The electrical and heating packages sit inside building services, which sits inside the main conversion contract. Optional wellness remains separate.

slides.title:
Make it
your mountain home.
slides.subtitle: OPTIONS & SELECTIONS
slides.body: Base €687,500. Premium furniture adds €16,000; wellness adds €34,800; terrace living adds €12,600. All selections together: €750,900, including contingency and excluding unpriced concealed conditions.

slides.title:
A thoughtful
transformation.
slides.subtitle: 07 / THE PROGRAMME
slides.body: An indicative 40-week project, with work sequencing shaped by surveys, permissions, long-lead glazing and Alpine weather. No delivery date is guaranteed by this fictional programme.

slides.title:
Before the
first opening-up.
slides.subtitle: SCOPE & DECISIONS
slides.body: Approve the design direction, investigate the actual building, resolve the technical design and select options before placing orders. A conversion begins with understanding what is already there.
points: All clients, suppliers, quotations and prices are fictional
Before and proposed images are generated concept studies
Plans are unmeasured and not for construction
Surveys, fees, specialist reports and exceptional repairs are excluded

slides.title:
Come for the mountains.
Stay for the feeling.
slides.subtitle: HAUS MORGENLICHT / DEMO 03
slides.body: An old Austrian chalet, opened to a new way of living. Prepared for the fictional Leitner family by Morgenlicht Atelier.
